draft.title: Energy flow diagrams
card: An energy flow diagram shows the forms of energy in a system, in order. Arrows join the forms and point from one form to the next.
A torch is drawn as: chemical energy in the battery, then electrical energy in the wires, then light and heat from the globe.
Each box names a form of energy. Each arrow shows a change from one form to another.
Most changes also give off some heat that is not wanted. It is drawn as an extra arrow leaving the main path.
draft.remember: Read a flow diagram arrow by arrow, and expect some unwanted heat to leave along the way.

a.q: What does an arrow in an energy flow diagram show?
opts: A change from one form of energy to the next
The size of the object that holds the energy
The place where the energy is finally used up
The time that each change in the system takes
a.why: An arrow joins two forms of energy and shows the change from one to the next. It does not show size or time. Energy is also not used up at the end, because it ends up in other forms.
a.clue: Look at what sits at each end of an arrow.

b.q: Isla charges her phone, then plays a video. Which flow diagram best fits the phone while it plays, including unwanted heat?
opts: Chemical to electrical to light and sound, with some heat
Electrical to chemical to light and sound, with no heat
Chemical to electrical to light and sound, with no heat
Light and sound to electrical to chemical, with some heat
b.why: The battery stores chemical energy, which becomes electrical energy and then light and sound from the screen and speaker. Most changes also give off some unwanted heat, so a diagram with no heat is incomplete. The order of the forms also matters.
b.clue: Start with where the energy is stored, and check whether heat is shown.

a.best: A change from one form of energy to the next

b.best: Chemical to electrical to light and sound, with some heat
